evidence:
Standard applied: workbook Quality Checks row 3 (#2) 'Keeps an authentic human voice (casual/terse is good); not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated prose', and skill quality-checks.md:14-15 (verify sentence variety, contractions, the occasional terse fragment in the notes; defect = uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, or a voice that changes between instruction.md and the notes). No internal annotation exists for this row. Not in read scope and not opened: deterministic-checks.md, the skill scripts, agents/openai.yaml, and the tests/solution trees (irrelevant to voice).

What supports Pass (task/instruction.md):
- It is a first-person request from a finance stakeholder throughout: line 1 opens 'Can you build HireOps into a compensation change desk?'; 24 first-person tokens (I/we/my/our/us/me) measured across the file.
- Sentence variety is real, not uniform cadence. Measured sentence lengths per paragraph: line 7 = [13, 48, 7, 25, 17] words; line 11 = [20, 16]; line 13 = [21, 4, 11, 23, 14, 11, 14]; line 15 = [17, 51, 14, 9, 23, 17]. Terse sentences sit beside long ones, e.g. line 7 'All of that before anything is saved.' (a fragment) and line 5 'the layout and names are yours'.
- Contractions and casual register are present: line 5 "We don't need a dashboard, theme switching or a special phone layout.", line 15 "How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call", "so don't install packages", "The server itself mustn't depend on any outside service".
- Zero marketing gloss: a regex for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|comprehensive|intuitive|streamlin|utilize|empower|crucial|furthermore|moreover returns no hit in instruction.md or either note. No bullets, numbered lists or headings in instruction.md, so no perfectly parallel bullets. One em dash, zero 'shall'.
- Idiomatic, situated phrasing that reads as a person describing their own work: line 1 'neither move can happen first', line 3 'without paying anyone twice', line 5 'so we can explain a change to an auditor', line 9 'Other people keep working while a change is open, so the desk has to keep up on its own.'
- Notes voice largely matches the brief. hireops_rules.md sections 1-9 are written in the same first-person plural with 81 contraction/possessive tokens and working anecdotes: line 19 "What keeps catching us out isn't any single screen.", line 53 "Routes, field names, element ids, button labels, the shape of the pages: all yours, we don't mind." (a terse fragment in the notes, exactly what the skill asks to see), line 190 'Trust the rows, not the sheet.', line 400-401 'so we can argue about where the number came from'.
- integration.md lines 1-14 are byte-for-byte the frozen template's integration.md lines 1-14 (compared directly); its impersonal register is template-controlled and is not attributed to the task author.

Residual observations that keep risk=true (bounded, none individually reaches the defect bar):
1. Register drift inside instruction.md. Lines 1-11 and 15 are conversational; lines 13 and 17 switch to clipped specification imperatives with slash-compounds and no requester voice: line 13 'Finance's coordinated changes need an ordinary form for selecting offers, destination requisitions and compensation terms, followed by a readable preview and commit/retry controls.' and 'A failed rescission request must retain its effective date for retry.'; line 17 'The operational requisition/offer/ledger rows are optional demonstration history, not a required import roster. An initially empty operational desk is acceptable.' These read as patched-in clarifications rather than the speaker of lines 1-11. Seven 'must' in 816 words.
2. Partial voice change between brief and notes. hireops_rules.md sections 10-12 (lines 415-558) and several inserted sentences (e.g. lines 84-88, 365-370) drop the 'we' voice for dense impersonal contract prose with slash-compounds ('grant/payment/referral' line 443-444, 'lines/after-images' line 471, 'recomputes/validates' line 462). Sections 1-9 keep the brief's voice, so this is a within-notes drift toward spec rather than a different speaker, and a rules note is expected to be more exact than the ask.
3. Spelling register differs between files: instruction.md uses British 'behaviour' (line 13), 'honour'/'honouring' (line 15); hireops_rules.md:420 uses 'Honor' and US -ize forms throughout ('amortized' line 20, 'annualized' line 117); integration.md:7 'honoring' is template text. A reader hunting for 'a voice that changes between instruction.md and the notes' could cite this. Spelling correctness itself belongs to row 3 and is not judged here.
4. A few polished antithesis constructions are the kind a strict reviewer associates with generated prose: line 7 'The change desk is somewhere we work, not just a form we submit.'; line 1 uses a colon-joined explanation. They are isolated and the surrounding text is plain.

Adversarial check as the assignment asks, translated to this row: a clearly failing brief (uniform ~18-word sentences, bulleted acceptance list, 'robust/seamless' gloss, no first person) is distinguishable from this text on every measured axis above, so the Pass is not vacuous. Conversely a genuinely human brief could be wrongly failed for items 1-3; I do not count them as a defect because the rubric explicitly allows terse writing and the dominant voice is consistent.

Limits: this is one reviewer's judgement on prose; no run or hosted QC result exists for this row and none is claimed. The hosted source reviewer may weigh items 1-3 differently, which is why risk is true.
suggested_fix: Optional, not required for Pass: in a future candidate, rephrase instruction.md lines 13 and 17 in the requester's own voice (e.g. 'Most of the old rows in the seed are just demo history, you don't have to import them; starting with an empty desk is fine') and align spelling register between instruction.md ('honour', 'behaviour') and hireops_rules.md:420 ('Honor'). Do not touch the template-controlled integration.md lines 1-14. Any such edit changes instruction bytes and invalidates current clearances.
